contributions.claim: The structural-semantic inversion: semantics-preserving transforms cause larger structural change than semantics-changing mutations, causing all representations to produce inverted similarity signals.

evidence.claim_registry: C009 — SUPPORTED, N=744, all 8 representations inverted
evidence.note: Retrospective finding from v1; pre-registration of resolution hypothesis (H9) completed in git commit 35b614c before v2 execution

prior_art.nearest_related: Jia & Harman mutation testing survey (2011) — mutation operators categorized but inversion phenomenon not quantified
prior_art.gap_reference: Agent 0E GAP-06: no prior work names or quantifies this phenomenon

contributions.sbg_delta: First empirical characterization of the structural-semantic inversion. No prior work in software similarity, clone detection, or mutation testing literature quantifies or names this phenomenon.
contributions.strongest_citation: C009 — All 8 baselines inverted, EQUIV_mean < CHANGED_mean, N=744, bootstrap CI all overlapping 0.5
weaknesses: Observed on a single benchmark (SBG Phase 1, Python programs, specific SP/SC operators)
Has not been replicated on Defects4J, Java programs, or other mutation operator sets
Mutation adequacy literature may contain related observations — not yet swept

contributions.claim: Execution-derived behavioral features resolve the structural-semantic inversion: dynamic AUROC=0.5310 with inversion delta=-0.0453 vs. v1 static delta=+0.0335.

evidence.note: AUROC=0.5310 resolves inversion directionally but remains below practical utility threshold and below best static baseline (AST=0.5528)

prior_art.closest: No prior work tests whether execution features resolve this specific inversion
related: Jiang & Su ISSTA 2009 — execution-based clone detection (does not address inversion)
McKeeman 1998 Differential Testing (binary divergence, does not address inversion)

contributions.sbg_delta: First empirical test of whether execution features correct the structural-semantic inversion. The question is novel because the inversion itself was not previously documented.
contributions.strongest_citation: PHASE_2_GATE.json: H7 SUPPORTED (CI [0.4991, 0.5806] entirely above v1=0.4237); H9 SUPPORTED (delta -0.0453 < 0 < 0.0335)
weaknesses: AUROC=0.5310 is still near-chance — clinical/practical utility threshold not met
H8 NOT SUPPORTED: hybrid with token-overlap proxy underperforms pure dynamic (0.4884 < 0.5310)

contributions.claim: Output-free behavioral genome: DynamicGenome uses only structural execution features (call frequency ranks, branch coverage consistency, exception type sets), explicitly excluding output values.

evidence.safeguard: SAFEGUARD-2 verified in 19-test PHASE_2_GATE test suite
evidence.test: SAFEGUARD-2: return_value and stdout absent from DynamicGenome

prior_art.closest: Jiang & Su ISSTA 2009 — I/O behavior vectors (uses output comparison directly)
prior_art.also: McKeeman 1998 Differential Testing — binary output comparison
prior_art.gap_reference: Agent 0E: SBG v2 must distinguish from Jiang & Su; SAFEGUARD-2 is the mechanism

contributions.sbg_delta: SBG V2 detects behavioral divergence through internal execution structure, not output values. Two programs can produce identical outputs while diverging in error handling, call patterns, or coverage — SBG V2 is sensitive to these; Jiang & Su and differential testing are not.
contributions.strongest_citation: v2 PHASE_2_GATE test: 'SAFEGUARD-2: return_value and stdout absent from DynamicGenome' — PASS
weaknesses: The output-free claim is only as strong as the feature audit; coverage-consistency and branch features may correlate with output correctness in simple cases
Empirical comparison against Jiang & Su on the same benchmark has not been run

contributions.claim: Formal pseudometric properties (symmetry, self-zero, bounded range) on execution-trace-derived behavioral features, formally specified and test-verified.

prior_art.closest: Walenstein et al. 2007 — informal behavioral distance via trace n-grams
prior_art.also: Christodorescu et al. S&P 2005 — behavioral templates (theorem-prover-based, not pseudometric)

contributions.sbg_delta: SBG V2 defines and tests formal pseudometric properties on execution-derived features. Prior behavioral fingerprinting works (TTAnalyze, Walenstein) use informal similarity measures without formal properties. The static CPG analogs (Joern, ProGraML) are not pseudometric systems.
contributions.strongest_citation: PHASE_2_GATE.json: all 3 pseudometric property tests pass; formal properties specified in HYPOTHESES_V2.md
weaknesses: The formal pseudometric claim is challenged by the security literature (Christodorescu 2005, Brumley 2008) which also formally defines behavioral distance
These prior works (GAP-05) are not currently in the prior art matrix

risks_summary.description: Jiang & Su (2009) is the most direct prior art for execution-based behavioral equivalence; its absence leaves a critical hole in the prior art review
McKeeman (1998) Differential Testing is the canonical execution-comparison prior art and is missing from the matrix
AUROC=0.5310 is marginally above chance; practical utility of the inversion resolution is limited
H8 NOT SUPPORTED — combining static and dynamic features hurts performance; the full genome may be less useful than individual dynamic features alone
C006 NOT SUPPORTED — ERROR_only (0.477) outperforms full 3-dim SBG (0.349); multi-dimensional combination may be counterproductive
Inversion finding may be benchmark-specific (Python, specific SP/SC operators); has not been replicated on independent benchmark
H11 cross-language: N=15 underpowered (~25% power), 3 of 8 dimensions excluded, no empirical result yet

recommended_framing: The structural-semantic inversion in software behavioral representations: characterization and execution-based resolution. We show that semantics-preserving transforms produce systematically larger structural change than semantics-altering mutations, causing all static and hybrid representations to fail on behavioral equivalence benchmarks. We then demonstrate that execution-derived behavioral features — output-free structural execution profiles — resolve this inversion (AUROC 0.4237→0.5310, inversion delta +0.0335→−0.0453), and identify the output-free design constraint as the key architectural requirement that separates behavioral genome detection from differential testing.
